title: Stock Option Calculator
description: Value stock options from strike price versus fair market value and share count.
howto: Enter the number of vested shares you can exercise.
Enter the strike (exercise) price and the current fair market value per share.
Choose ISO or NSO for the tax note.
Read the cost to exercise, the spread value, and the break-even price.

faqs.a: Fair market value minus strike price, times shares. It is the paper gain you capture by exercising.
The FMV is below the strike price, so exercising now would lose money. The spread shows as negative.

faqs.q: How are ISOs and NSOs taxed differently?
faqs.a: Broadly: NSOs are taxed as ordinary income on the spread at exercise; ISOs can qualify for capital-gains treatment if holding rules are met but may trigger AMT. See a tax professional.
